why: (review round 2, B.1; retargeted in review round 3 to the clamp that replaced min(1.4rem, 19cqi)) the long figure back to a fixed 1.4rem: at a 24px default font '12,345,678' overruns its tile
(review round 2, B.2) .long leaves the shared rule: no min-height or bottom alignment, so beside a three-digit figure its label sits higher than its neighbour's
(review round 2, B.3) the threshold at nine characters: '1,234,567' (nine) loses the long class and wraps at the narrow widths
(review round 2, B.4) the measured guard removed: an unmeasured tile's words ('no count for last night') get the long class and overflow their tile
(review round 3, B.1) the 1rem floor removed, min(1.4rem, 16.5cqi): at a 24px default font the figure is below the body text at 1920px and 390px, and the size-floor assertion goes red
(review round 3, B.1) N back to 19cqi: at the default font at 1280px the figure is 22.4px, 5.00em wide, and its width times 1.15 runs past its 122.6px tile
(review round 3, B.3) no <wbr> after the commas: the long figure has no break point, so where the floor is wider than the tile it runs past it, and the SSR test and the break assertion go red
(review round 3, B.3) a <wbr> after every digit, not only after a comma: the SSR test's count of break points goes red
(review round 3, B.5) the shared rule without align-items: a long figure's text sits at the top of its box, so its bottom is not level with 345's, and the bottom-level assertion goes red
(review round 3, B.4) the 1.4rem fallback line before the clamp removed: a browser without container units would drop the declaration and fall to the inherited size; the SSR CSS pin goes red

(review round 4, major 1) the span removed, the pieces straight in the flex p: each run between the wbrs is a flex item on one line that cannot wrap, as Firefox lays it out. The SSR pin (the only child is a span) goes red

(review round 4, tests 2) the 1,234,567 ratio back to the one 1.15 margin: at 390px and 24px the estimate says one line (106.9 x 1.15 = 122.9 in a 126px tile) where Pragmatica wraps it (129px); the shipped-font check goes red

(review round 4, tests 1) the per-line estimate without the figure ratio: a wrapped figure's lines are then the fallback's lines, and 390px at 24px (120px in a 126px tile) stays one line, so the wrapped branch finds no break to check
